summary:
Physics and nav are finished and green: `npx vitest run` passes 138 of 138 tests (physics 75, nav 50, foundation 13 untouched), and the type-check of my directories prints nothing. The suite passed 13 consecutive runs, 4 of them with eight busy-loop processes saturating the 4 cores.

**The failing allocation test was right; the implementation allocated.**
- `moveAndSlide` boxed three numbers (48 bytes) on every call as soon as a second CollisionWorld instance existed. With a single world V8 constant-folds the module constants and the problem disappears, which is why the earlier scratch experiments looked clean.
- The cause was the delta clamp (`dx > MAX_DELTA ? MAX_DELTA : dx`): it mixes a raw double with a constant V8 can no longer fold, so the value is kept as a heap number.
- Fixed with `Math.min`/`Math.max`, and the raycast results are now written field by field instead of through `Vector3.set()`.
- DIAG instrumentation is removed. The check is now a shared meter (`src/physics/heapmeter.ts`) that needs no `--expose-gc` and takes the median of |heap growth| per call over 41 short rounds. A collection can only push the reading toward "allocates".
- A positive control (one boxed number per call) reads 16.13 bytes; every clean query reads 0.13-0.28 against a limit of 2. Run against the unfixed implementation, the new test fails with "moveAndSlide (steady walk) allocates about 48.2 bytes per call".

**Other physics changes**
- **Behaviour change:** a body that clears a low rim in one stride, with no floor within snap reach behind it, now hops it and continues airborne at its original height. Before, it stopped dead as if it had hit a wall.
- The candidate region now covers the full snap reach below multi-step moves.
- New tests: diagonal stairs up and down at 30/60/144 Hz, the rim hop, a crouched body under a beam, a floor switched off under a body, and hundreds of boxes in one spot.
- An inherited test compared the shared result object with itself, so it could not fail; it now does its job.

**Nav changes** (it had never been tested)
- `nearestWalkable` could loop effectively forever on a huge radius or far-away position; the search is now clipped to the grid.
- `findPath` boxed four numbers per call; it now uses integer A* costs and passes no coordinates through helper calls.
- String pulling now takes the farthest visible point by bisection. Before, an open-floor path with the goal in plain view got a spurious extra waypoint.
- Flow sampling used to cut within 0.29 m of a wall corner at tight turns; it now crosses through the middle of the cell border when no straight shot has clearance.
- Grid edge is capped at 512 cells (was 2048), because the flow field keeps 18 ints per cell.

**Nav test coverage** (`src/nav/nav.test.ts`)
- Every cell and every link of a hand-built level (two rooms, S-bend corridor, stair-reached terrace, two gates) is compared with an independent reference built from collision queries. The same is done for nine hint variations and three random arenas.
- Flow distances are checked against a reference shortest-path search for many targets, with gates open and closed.
- 60-agent simulations at 0.05, 0.12 and 0.32 m steps: all arrive, none ever stands in an unwalkable cell, and none oscillates (the flow distance never climbs back and there are never two reversals within 12 steps).
- Also covered: a closed gate holding agents back, a moving target, and box-shaped agents driven by `moveAndSlide` through the real geometry and up the stairs.
- Paths, annulus sampling, region toggles, unreachable and off-mesh cases, and allocation are tested too.

**Measured performance** (150 x 90 grid, 419 boxes, 11 574 walkable cells)

| Operation | Measured | Asserted |
|---|---|---|
| Flow field rebuild | median 0.37 ms | best quartile < 2 ms, median < 10 ms |
| `sampleFlow` | 1.3 us (60 agents: 0.08 ms per frame) | < 15 us |
| `findPath` | 130 us | < 2500 us |
| Nav build | 6 ms | < 600 ms |
| `moveAndSlide` (5000 boxes) | 0.38 us | < 25 us |
| `raycast` (5000 boxes) | 1.1 us | < 25 us |

Deliberately broken copies of the implementations were run against the suites: 25 of 30 nav bugs and 15 of 18 physics bugs are caught. Of the eight survivors, six leave results unchanged (redundant checks or pure optimisations); the other two are an agent-height check that the flood fill's passage test duplicates, and a tie order the contract leaves open.

gates.typecheck: PASS - `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E "^src/(physics|nav)/"` prints nothing (the whole project currently reports 0 TS errors).
gates.unitTests: PASS - `npx vitest run`: 3 files, 138 passed, 0 failed (src/physics/collision.test.ts 75, src/nav/nav.test.ts 50, src/core/foundation.test.ts 13, not edited). 13 consecutive green runs, 4 of them under CPU saturation, plus one with --pool=threads. Suite takes about 8 s.
gates.build: Not run (assignment forbids npm run build).
gates.smoke: Not run (no browser or harness check was part of this assignment).
gates.campaign: Not run (not part of this assignment).

contractRequests: Low priority: queries that return a bare number (CollisionWorld.groundHeight, NavGrid.heightAt, NavGrid.flowDistance) can cost one boxed number (12-16 bytes) per call when V8 does not inline them, and callers passing fractional coordinates to scalar-argument queries (groundHeight, heightAt, isWalkable, cellAt, zoneAt) can have those boxed too. In my measurements they were normally inlined and cost nothing; I saw flowDistance at 15 bytes per call once. If strict zero garbage matters for ground enemies, add Vec3Like-in / out-param variants such as heightAt(pos, fallback).

Low priority: overlapBoxAll(box, mask, out: number[]) must leave out.length equal to the count ('cleared first'), so V8 reallocates the array's backing store whenever the count grows again after shrinking. Either state that only out[0..count-1] is valid and the length may stay larger, or accept the occasional resize; with a stable result size it allocates nothing.

Documentation: NavGrid.setRegionWalkable and NavBuildHints.closedRegions only affect cells whose centre lies inside the region. A gate region that covers no cell centre (thinner than a cell and off-centre) blocks nothing, so world gate regions must be at least one cell thick and cover the centres. The current skeleton gates (1 m thick, centred on a cell border) do, because the comparison is inclusive.

Documentation: NavBuildHints.maxStep (0.75) is larger than PLAYER.STEP_UP (0.45). The grid links neighbouring cells whose floors differ by up to 0.75 m, so ground enemies moved with moveAndSlide need stepUp 0.75 wherever the world has a single riser between 0.45 and 0.75 m. Stairs with 0.2 m risers are fine with any stepUp of 0.2 or more.
openIssues: Behaviour change for player and enemy owners: a body that clears a low rim in one stride, with no floor within snap reach behind it, now hops over and is left airborne at its original height instead of being reported as a wall hit. This needs a single-frame advance of about body width plus rim thickness (a 0.8 m dash frame for the player; a normal run for bodies about 0.2 m wide). At walking pace nothing changes.

Off-mesh steering goes by distance only: sampleFlow sends an agent standing in an unwalkable cell toward the nearest cell centre (within 3 m) that leads to the target, even when that cell is on the other side of a thin wall. This is pinned by a test using the sealed closet.

Flow directions can turn sharply in a single frame at corners (up to roughly 90-130 degrees). There is no oscillation, and left-right wobble stays under 0.35 events per 1000 steps at running pace on the arenas the suite asserts on. A consumer that wants smooth facing should rate-limit yaw.

The allocation results were measured only in Node 22 (V8 12.4) under vitest, in the harder multi-instance mode. Nothing was run in a browser. Chrome uses pointer compression (a boxed number is 12 bytes there), which the calibrated control accounts for, but that is untested.
src/physics/heapmeter.ts is test support that lives in src/ so both suites can share it. Nothing in the game imports it.
Flow field memory is 18 Int32 per cell (0.97 MB at 150 x 90). Grids larger than 512 cells on an edge are silently truncated; this was 2048 before.
Both test files set a 120 s per-test timeout. Under 3x CPU oversubscription one nav test exceeded vitest's default 5 s before I lightened it and raised the limit.
